Package com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest

Class SinglesColumnChecks

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest.SinglesColumnChecks
public final class SinglesColumnChecks extends Object
Singles support and gravity in a live level that does not touch loader-native automation directly: grounding at the bottom of a column, a cell resting on the one below it, visual columns lining up across differently rotated blocks, and extraction shifting a column down while carrying each item's rotation with it. Capability/Transfer-API-facing tests stay in each loader's own SinglesColumnGameTests.

  • Method Details

    • standaloneBottomIsGroundedAndFloatingCellIsRejected

      public static void standaloneBottomIsGroundedAndFloatingCellIsRejected(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The bottom layer stands on the world, while an unsupported higher cell rejects a deposit. To reproduce in-game: aim at an empty bottom cell and deposit, then aim at a higher cell with nothing beneath it. Only the bottom deposit succeeds.

    • upperCellUsesTheCellImmediatelyBelow

      public static void upperCellUsesTheCellImmediatelyBelow(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A Singles item is supported by the cell directly beneath it. To reproduce in-game: deposit into a bottom cell, then the same visual column one layer higher. Both items remain stacked.

    • differentlyRotatedBlocksShareVisualSeamColumns

      public static void differentlyRotatedBlocksShareVisualSeamColumns(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Support across a block seam follows visual columns despite different block rotations. To reproduce in-game: rotate two stacked Singles blocks differently, fill a top cell of the lower block, then deposit into the visually aligned bottom cell above. The deposit succeeds.

    • extractionShiftsOneColumnAndCarriesItemRotation

      public static void extractionShiftsOneColumnAndCarriesItemRotation(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Extraction shifts only the aimed visual column down one layer and carries item rotations. To reproduce in-game: make a three-item vertical Singles column, rotate the upper two items, and extract the bottom item. The other two descend with their orientations unchanged.

    • shiftKeepsAnItemItWouldNoLongerAccept

      public static void shiftKeepsAnItemItWouldNoLongerAccept(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Validity gates insertion only, so an item stored before the rule narrowed under it has to survive the shift that closes the gap beneath it. An ingot stands in for such an item: a Singles Stack refuses one from a deposit, because Bar accepts it, but may be holding one that predates an ss ingot edit or a data pack reload.

      To reproduce in-game: store an item in Singles, change the ingot list so Singles would now reject it, place another item below it, and extract the lower item. The newly rejected stored item moves down rather than being lost.

    • drawDownKeepsAnItemItWouldNoLongerAccept

      public static void drawDownKeepsAnItemItWouldNoLongerAccept(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The same conservation across a block boundary: the item handed down from the block above is one the receiving block would refuse from a deposit.

      To reproduce in-game: store an item in the bottom cell of an upper Singles block, change the ingot list so Singles rejects it, and extract the aligned top item below. The stored item crosses the seam rather than being lost.

    • extractionPreservesAnExistingGap

      public static void extractionPreservesAnExistingGap(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Singles gravity shifts occupied cells exactly one layer and does not compact a preexisting gap. To reproduce in-game: use automation to leave a gap between two items in one column, then extract the bottom item. The gap remains and the upper item descends only one layer.

    • extractionDrawsAcrossDifferentlyRotatedBlockBoundary

      public static void extractionDrawsAcrossDifferentlyRotatedBlockBoundary(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Extraction draws from the visually aligned column across a differently rotated block seam. To reproduce in-game: rotate two stacked Singles blocks differently, put items across one visual seam column, rotate the upper item, and extract the lower item. The upper item crosses the seam with its item rotation intact and its emptied block disappears.

    • depositTraceStopsAtLastEmptyBeforeOccupiedCell

      public static void depositTraceStopsAtLastEmptyBeforeOccupiedCell(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A deposit ray stops at the last empty cell before an occupied cell. To reproduce in-game: place an item deeper in a Singles row and aim through the empty cells toward it. The new item occupies the empty cell immediately in front of the stored item.

    • depositTraceUsesFarthestCellWhenNothingIsOccupied

      public static void depositTraceUsesFarthestCellWhenNothingIsOccupied(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      An unobstructed deposit ray selects its farthest supported cell. To reproduce in-game: aim through an entirely empty supported Singles row and deposit. The item appears in the farthest cell on that ray.

    • breakingMiddleBlockDropsItsContentsWithoutClosingTheGap

      public static void breakingMiddleBlockDropsItsContentsWithoutClosingTheGap(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Breaking the middle Singles block drops only its local items and does not pull the upper block through the new gap. To reproduce in-game: put one distinct item in the same column of each block in a three-block Singles run and break the middle block. Its item drops and the upper item stays in the upper block.

    • comparatorReservesZeroForAnEmptyColumn

      public static void comparatorReservesZeroForAnEmptyColumn(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The comparator range reserves 0 for an empty column, as a vanilla container's does, and a cell holds one item, so full means every cell of every block occupied.

      To reproduce in-game: compare an empty Singles column, the same column with one item, and a full column. Their comparator outputs are 0, at least 1, and 15 respectively.

    • comparatorReadsTheWholeColumnFromEveryBlock

      public static void comparatorReadsTheWholeColumnFromEveryBlock(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Every block in a Singles column reports the same whole-column fill. To reproduce in-game: make a two-block column with one block's cells full and the other empty, then place comparators against both blocks. Both report the half-full value.

    • comparatorFollowsAColumnLosingABlock

      public static void comparatorFollowsAColumnLosingABlock(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The fill is measured against the column's current height, so a run that loses a block reports the same contents as a larger share of a smaller column.

      To reproduce in-game: fill the lower half of a two-block Singles column, read its comparator, then remove the empty upper block. The lower block's output rises from half full to full.
